chapter: In The Mood, Rendezvous and Capitol
title: Firing Artis Paul in Las Vegas and the union hearing
summary: Fields pays off drunk Artis Paul rather than use him in Las Vegas; Artis files charges and then confirms Fields' account.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: We headed back along into Tulsa and while we're talking about the incident, Artis Paul we were talking about--what made me think about it is in Arizona when this happened, and I had told Artis and told Artis, Artis, if you get drunk again, that's it, I'm just paying you off. You're not supposed to get drunk and I've been telling you and I've been putting up with it; I'm just going to pay you off then and there.

We were to play Las Vegas, it was only a one nighter, but you know, to say you played in Las Vegas is very, very important, and so just before we went in there, Artis got drunk. I handed him his money, I don't know
what it was but I said this is it, and he said, I can't ride in? We were headed in to headquarters, and I said sure you're welcome to, but you're not working.

He said now I know I had a little too much, but he said you know I don't want to let you down, we're all good friends, you and all the rest of the band, I know you want me in Las Vegas tomorrow night. I said I can do without you tomorrow night, I'm going to do without you until we get somebody, so he just kept on begging and begging and I went on into Las Vegas and wouldn't use him.
We played without him and went on and I played--
How many trumpets did you have then?
I had three, and we just went on and did the job with two--I had two
or three dates before we got back into Tulsa and played them.

So when I got in, Artis filed charges against him, that I let him out and didn't give him his notice, and so I answered them and told them yes, I told him and told him and it's a rule when he came with the band, that if he was drunk, I didn't allow that and I said that was the condition that he was working in. If he disobeys those--he couldn't work that night, that night he couldn't do anything and so I'll have to give him credit for this. So when they showed him this--it was a rebuttal-- Artis said, he's telling the truth.
He said it was exactly right.
We got along after that. He said you really meant it.
